macros.AbstractAblation: Fresh predictor removal increases planner Brier by $+0.0846$ (95\% CI $[+0.0479,+0.1225]$).
macros.AblationFinding: Fresh removal changes A1 Brier by $+0.0846$ (95\% CI $[+0.0479,+0.1225]$) and A2 by $+0.0831$ (95\% CI $[+0.0473,+0.1197]$). This tests access to the predictor, including the induced change in tool policy. Fresh A1 controls call $B^\star$ in 470/471 trajectories, versus none without access. Across repeats, A1 Brier ranges from 0.2348 to 0.2365 with access and 0.2911 to 0.3509 without it.
macros.VerificationFinding: In fresh controls, 7/471 outputs change (3 improve, 4 worsen), with A2--A1 $+0.00033$ (95\% CI $[-0.00008,+0.00092]$); without the predictor, 16/471 change (7 improve, 9 worsen), with $-0.00120$ (95\% CI $[-0.00722,+0.00406]$). Of these, 1 change involves a prior fallback (marked in Figure~\ref{fig:results}D); trace analysis separates fallback from valid revisions.
macros.TemporalFinding: All six calendar-block intervals for predictor removal remain above zero.
macros.ExecutionFinding: The fresh ablation uses 3,463 calls with 0 transport failures and 5 fallback outputs across 1,884 predictions; its inference allocation is 14.35 GPU-hours.
macros.PreparationFinding: A separate exact replay of shared offline preparation takes 9.41\,s; fresh $B^\star$ warm service takes 140.99\,ms median, including packet preparation.
macros.ConclusionAblation: The access intervention supports dependence on the conventional predictor; these results do not establish an orchestration advantage beyond that predictor.
